# Sleep Study

**Authors:** Brian Gerstenslager, Jennifer M. Slowik

**Source:** StatPearls - StatPearls Publishing

## Abstract

A polysomnogram (PSG), also known to patients as a sleep study, is an integral component of many sleep evaluations. Attended (Type I) PSGs are the gold standard for diagnosing sleep-related breathing disorders (SRBD), including obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). Many other sleep disorders can also be diagnosed and managed based on PSG results. The study consists of a simultaneous recording of several physiologic parameters during sleep and wakefulness, including the electroencephalogram (EEG) to identify wake versus sleep and its stages.  This article focuses on sleep center-based, attended PSG, where the patient must stay overnight at a specialized sleep laboratory. This article will provide an overview of the processes of obtaining and interpreting the attended PSG as a part of the diagnosis and management of a wide range of sleep complaints.
